# Freedom with AI

> Freedom with AI provides strategic advisory for founders building across the AI stack. Founders work directly with Sonia Sarao or Cammie Clay.

The firm works across industries, especially where products, buying decisions, operations or regulation are complex.

## Thesis

[Thesis](https://freedomwith.ai/thesis): AI companies depend on energy, chips, infrastructure, models and applications. Each layer has different technology, capital needs, margins and paths to market. Models range from proprietary frontier systems to open-source and domain-specific alternatives. Applications include software as well as scientific tools, robots, vehicles and other systems that can sense, decide and act. Freedom with AI works at the company-building layer, helping founders turn technical capability into a product, a market and a durable business. The five-layer stack builds on Jensen Huang's framing of AI as infrastructure. The company-building layer reflects the firm's own work with founders.

## Advisory

[Advisory](https://freedomwith.ai/advisory) is the main business. Engagements begin with a three- or six-month term and are shaped around the company's priorities and the decisions in motion.

## Advisors

- Sonia Sarao: Strategic advisor with additional depth across product, technology, growth and AI. She led products and teams through growth and acquisition and now builds faibuddy, a live AI-native product for founders. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/sonia-sarao/
- Cammie Clay: Strategic advisor with additional depth across regulation, risk, governance and stakeholder strategy. She was a regulator at the New York Stock Exchange and FINRA, then a compliance executive at RS Investments and First Republic Bank. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/cammieclay/

## Other work

- [faibuddy](https://faibuddy.com) is the firm's AI advisory product for founders.
- The firm is beginning to make a small number of angel investments in founder-led companies across the AI stack, where it has conviction and can be useful beyond the capital. Advisory and investment decisions are separate: working with the firm neither requires nor guarantees an investment.
